elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: its contractors acting on Licensee's behalf
No perpetuity language added; grant remains "subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and provided that Licensee makes payments"

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: Licensee may, upon written notice to Licensor and without Licensor's consent, transfer this Agreement ... to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition

offending_extra_words: Licensee's Affiliates and contractors acting on Licensee's behalf shall not be deemed third parties for purposes of the restrictions in this Agreement, and Licensee shall remain responsible for their compliance with this Agreement
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the redline omits three preferred atomic elements: perpetuity and irrevocability of paid-up licences, and the limitation of subscription termination to uncured material breach.

The clause as edited does sit at the fallback: affiliates are covered (indeed granted directly, better than notice-based coverage) and transfer to an M&A successor is permitted without consent, with an express statement that no such transaction terminates or suspends the licence.

Minimality fails: the official gate flags operation 1 expanding 16 words to 25 (ratio 1.56), and the inserted limb (i) duplicates the affiliate/contractor protection already achieved in the grant sentence; a single tighter insertion would suffice.
"reorganization" broadens the transfer trigger beyond the fallback's M&A framing and is not needed to complete the level.

Unrelated terms (Field of Use, payment condition, assignment consent mechanics) remain effective; the "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary" opener resolves the tension with restriction (e) and Article XX without creating a dangling mechanic.
